newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE IN MILLION DOLLAR FORM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE IN MILLION DOLLAR FORM.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie shrugged off the memories of second-to-last finishes in his two previous appearances to lead the Million Dollar Challenge after a first round 65 on Friday.
Europe's top golfer carded five birdies and an eagle three at the par-five ninth to head the 12-strong field by two shots in the rain-delayed tournament.
"It's nice to be in the running here for the first time and not just playing for a place at the back of the pack," Montgomerie said.
"This is the best I've played since the Lancome Trophy in September. I don't really know why. I think it's helped that I took two weeks off before this event and I simply just relaxed."
Montgomerie's was the lowest opening round score in the 16-year history of the event.

World number four Ernie Els, looking for his first Million Dollar win at his fifth attempt, filled joint second place with U.S. Open Stever Jones and said that he had been motivated by Montgomerie's excellent round.
"I was just keeping up with Colin. He was firing the pins out at every hole. I had a good par-save at the fifth and that really picked me up."
Els said the course was in tremendous shape: "These greens are very receptive as they're still quite soft and I think we're going to get some low scoring this afternoon."
Sun City debutants Steve Stricker and Mark Brooks of the United States were one shot back on 68, along with previous winner Ian Woosnam and defending champion Corey Pavin.
